title: Card lookup keeps the smallest unique covering card
summary: A spoken card match requires every content token of the query to sit in the card. The smallest unique card wins. A tie, or a miss, is no answer.
body:
The card loader documents the spoken match as a covering lookup. Every content token of the query has to be in the card, and the smallest unique haystack wins. A tie is not a guess. The public lookup follows that rule. A query that yields no content token produces no hit. If any token is missing from the index, the lookup returns nothing, which is a miss. Candidates that contain every token are ordered by how many distinct tokens the card holds, and then by id. When the first two share that same count, the lookup returns nothing rather than picking either card. An empty gist is also no answer.

The retrieve module states the same predicate for a hit haystack: every content token of the query must be present, and an empty term list does not match. The loader reads cards. It does not write a card. A card with research_only set, or not_for containing answer, is not indexed and cannot be spoken as a fact. The field rules it applies are the knowledge-card rules: an id, a title, a body, a section, a category, a claim type, an evidence label, who said it, a date, a status, sources, contested views, and related ids.
